newsitem.title: USA: US FERC delays action on gas pipeline market test.
newsitem.headline: US FERC delays action on gas pipeline market test.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday delayed decisions on 12 companies' plans to lift price caps on rates charged for released pipeline capacity in a pilot program that was supposed to begin November 1.

Up to now the commission has blocked natural gas shippers from charging more than a pipeline's regulated rates when they rent to other shippers space which they have reserved on interstate pipelines -- the so-called secondary market.
Under the pilot program, the commission wanted to test whether lifting price caps in the secondary market would help spur more efficient pricing and better use of pipeline space.

The pilot program was proposed in July at the same time as the commission allowed pipelines to charge market-based rates, as opposed to regulated rates, for interruptible and short-term firm capacity, which compete with released space.

FERC staff said pilot program approvals were delayed because the commission wanted to ensure that the companies proposing to lift price caps could not get away with charging exorbitant rates in their areas.
